To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the 10- 10 electrode array and digital analysis of EEG data provide better concordant results between MEG and the EEG.
MEG spikes not detected by EEG are often of low voltage and can be detected by digital EEG analysis.
MEG can detect spikes that are not visible in the concomitant EEG.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the detection of epileptic activity in the human brain by magnetoencephalograpy and electroencephalogram (EEG).
the detection of epileptic discharges in the MEG and EEG recordings in patients with epilepsy.
the development of a method to improve the yield of EEG recordings in patients with epilepsy.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the MEG data are not only more sensitive for the detection of spikes than the EEG data but also more reliable.
MEG is a better tool than EEG for the detection of spikes in the Landau-Kleffer syndrome.
MEG is superior to EEG for the detection of spikes in the epileptogenic focus.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

MEG and EEG are complementary techniques for the investigation of epileptic spike activity and that the combination of MEG with the 10- 10 electrode system provides the most sensitive method of spike detection in patients with Landau-Klefner syndrome.
MEG is superior to conventional EEG for spike detection.
the use of the 122 channel MEG system is an excellent adjunct to the conventional EEG for the detection and localization of epileptogenic spikes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
MEG is more sensitive than EEG in detecting epileptogenic spikes, and that modern EEG analysis methods are more sensitive than conventional methods.
the 10- 10 system of EEG electrode placement combined with modern digital data analysis techniques can provide better concurrence with the MEG data.
the 10- 20 system of electrode location does not provide an optimal data set for MEG-EEGs and that modern methods of digital analysis are needed to improve data concordance.
